source.locator: lines 9-16, closing sentence of the part editorial

findings.finding: The phrase `is at planning to work` is ungrammatical and interrupts an otherwise direct statement of a contributor's plan.
findings.controlling_evidence: Removing the stray `at` yields the grammatical construction `is planning to work` while preserving the named person, issue reference, and editorial intent.
findings.required_translation_handling: Translate the intended `is planning to work`, preserve issue 65, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-001 disclosure.

findings.finding: The remark says every subset N of the domain determines a substructure, including the empty subset.
findings.controlling_evidence: OpenLogic's structure definition requires a non-empty domain; the stated construction is therefore a structure only when N is non-empty.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add only the condition N not equal to the empty set, keep the relation restriction unchanged, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-002 disclosure.

findings.finding: The value of t in M-prime is expanded using the interpretation of f in M rather than in M-prime.
findings.controlling_evidence: The left side is `\Value{t}{M'}[h \circ s]`, the argument values are all in M-prime, and the immediately following calculation correctly uses `\Assign{f}{M'}`.
findings.required_translation_handling: Change only the affected interpretation superscript from M to M-prime and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-003 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 61-70, alternating construction of partial isomorphisms

findings.finding: At an even stage the source writes n+1=2r and adds b_r. The first such stage is n+1=2, so the construction starts with b_1 and never forces b_0 into the range.
findings.controlling_evidence: Writing n=2r+1 for the even branch makes its successive choices b_0, b_1, and so on, parallel to the odd branch's a_0, a_1, and so on.
findings.required_translation_handling: Replace only the branch parametrization by n=2r+1, retain b_r, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-005 disclosure.

findings.finding: The proposition calls the language purely relational while explicitly allowing constants, contradicting this section's earlier definition of purely relational as having predicates only and no functions or constants.
findings.controlling_evidence: The proposition's mathematical content explicitly lists finitely many predicate and constant symbols and no function symbols; that inventory can be stated directly without the conflicting label.
findings.required_translation_handling: State the listed signature conditions directly, omit only the conflicting `purely relational` label here, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-006 disclosure.

findings.finding: The definition uses n both for the recursion level I_n and for the independently varying sequence length. In the I_0 clause this would restrict the displayed variable list to length zero.
findings.controlling_evidence: I_n is defined on all pairs of equal-length finite sequences; assigning their common length a separate name k makes the atomic variable list x_1 through x_k.
findings.required_translation_handling: Name the common sequence length k, change only the atomic variable-list endpoint from n to k, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-007 disclosure.

source.locator: lines 122-129 and 199-203, finite-rank proposition and its converse-proof use

findings.finding: The proposition establishes finiteness only for sentences, but the converse proof invokes finiteness for formulas B(x,y-vector). It also calls the syntactic set T finite rather than finite up to logical equivalence.
findings.controlling_evidence: For a finite relational-and-constant signature, fixed quantifier rank, and fixed finite list of possible free variables, there are finitely many formula equivalence classes. Their satisfied representatives have a finite conjunction, which is the formula the proof needs.
findings.required_translation_handling: State the standard fixed-variable formula-class lemma with the sentence result as k=0, use a finite conjunction of satisfied representatives in the proof, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-008 disclosure.

findings.finding: The three order-position cases presuppose a non-empty partial map and a new point a. They cover neither p empty nor a already in the domain of p.
findings.controlling_evidence: If p is empty, any singleton order-preserving map supplies the required extension; if a is already in its domain, q=p suffices. The source's three cases then cover every genuinely new point for non-empty p.
findings.required_translation_handling: Add those two preliminary cases, retain the source's three new-point position cases, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-009 disclosure.

findings.finding: The exercise claims every definable subset is fixed by every automorphism without restricting parameters. A set defined using a movable parameter need not be invariant under an automorphism that moves that parameter.
findings.controlling_evidence: A parameter-free defining formula is preserved by every automorphism. More generally a definition with parameters is preserved only by automorphisms fixing those parameters, but the exercise quantifies over an arbitrary automorphism.
findings.required_translation_handling: Restrict the exercise to a subset definable without additional parameters, retain the invariance equation, and add an adjacent OLTEMODBAS-010 disclosure.
